With relatively few radiometric dates available, most workers have had to rely upon field criteria and composition to attempt a classification of the intrusions. Commonly these were grouped, from oldest to youngest, as acidic, intermediate, basic and alkaline intrusions. In the course of three field seasons we have collected samples from some 200 sites in the igneous rocks. The results to date suggest that the majority of these, including most of the acidic, intermediate and basic intrusions, are associated with the closing stages of the Pan-African event (Davies et al., 1980). The remaining, younger rocks include some which were emplaced since the mid to late Cretaceous and which constitute the subject of this paper. Thermomagnetic analysis Alkaline and basic-acid rock samples from all the studied units were analyzed with a thermomagnetic balance for the determination of Curie temperatures (T,) and the identification of magnetic minerals. For all alkaline rocks the thermomagnetic curves were similar and, in general, two magnetic phases were observed. The first one with transition temperatures between 350 and 450°C probably indicates the pres- ence of maghemite, whereas the second with Curie temperatures between 570 and 594°C is characteris- tic of titanomagnetites with a composition close to that of magnetite (Fig. 7a-c). For tinguaites from the Poses de Caldas complex, the Curie temperatures were not well defined (Fig. 7d) due to superposition of paramagnetic effects from the matrix on the ferri- magnetic mineral signal. section_candidates.excerpt: Itatiaia complex The Itatiaia alkaline complex (220 km’, Fig. 2) is located on the boundary between the states of Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais. This intrudes into the Precambrian basement, which is represented by the Juiz de Fora metamorphic complex [7,17]. The Itati- aia massif is structurally linked to the SE Brazilian continental rift, which developed in an ENE to EW trending transcurrent system by the end of the BrasiI- iano (Pan African) Cycle and which was reactivated during the breakup of Gondwana [18]. The alkaline complex is composed of syenites, foyaites, pulask- ites, quartz syenites, magmatic breccias and alkaline granite [19]. The mean K-Ar age obtained on ten biotites from the Itatiaia rocks is 70.5 f 3.3 Ma [10,12]. 2.3. Passa Quatro complex The Passa Quatro alkaline complex (148 km*, Fig. 2) is close to the Itatiaia complex. It was emplaced into the Precambrian metamorphic com- plexes of Juiz de Fora, Paraiba do Sul and the Aqungui Group [7,17]. The main lithological types are alkali plutonic rocks (nepheline syenites) with minor phonolitic dykes. section_candidates.excerpt: Itatiaia complex The Itatiaia alkaline complex (220 km’, Fig. 2) is located on the boundary between the states of Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais. This intrudes into the Precambrian basement, which is represented by the Juiz de Fora metamorphic complex [7,17]. The Itati- aia massif is structurally linked to the SE Brazilian continental rift, which developed in an ENE to EW trending transcurrent system by the end of the BrasiI- iano (Pan African) Cycle and which was reactivated during the breakup of Gondwana [18]. The alkaline complex is composed of syenites, foyaites, pulask- ites, quartz syenites, magmatic breccias and alkaline granite [19]. The mean K-Ar age obtained on ten biotites from the Itatiaia rocks is 70.5 f 3.3 Ma [10,12]. 2.3. Passa Quatro complex The Passa Quatro alkaline complex (148 km*, Fig. 2) is close to the Itatiaia complex. It was emplaced into the Precambrian metamorphic com- plexes of Juiz de Fora, Paraiba do Sul and the Aqungui Group [7,17]. The main lithological types are alkali plutonic rocks (nepheline syenites) with minor phonolitic dykes. Experimental procedure and results Silo Sebastib Island is located along the south- east coast of the state of Sb Paul0 (Fig. 3). It is composed of Precambrian granitic rocks that were modified by the Brasiliano Cycle and it is intruded by Early Cretaceous subalkaline basic-acid dykes and by Late Cretaceous alkaline stocks and dykes ([24] and references therein). The Early Cretaceous dykes have a northeasterly trend and are of variable thickness (2-50 m) and extent (2-15 km). These dykes are cut by alkaline stocks (syenites). section_candidates.excerpt: Itatiaia complex The Itatiaia alkaline complex (220 km’, Fig. 2) is located on the boundary between the states of Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais. This intrudes into the Precambrian basement, which is represented by the Juiz de Fora metamorphic complex [7,17]. The Itati- aia massif is structurally linked to the SE Brazilian continental rift, which developed in an ENE to EW trending transcurrent system by the end of the BrasiI- iano (Pan African) Cycle and which was reactivated during the breakup of Gondwana [18]. The alkaline complex is composed of syenites, foyaites, pulask- ites, quartz syenites, magmatic breccias and alkaline granite [19]. The mean K-Ar age obtained on ten biotites from the Itatiaia rocks is 70.5 f 3.3 Ma [10,12]. 2.3. Passa Quatro complex The Passa Quatro alkaline complex (148 km*, Fig. 2) is close to the Itatiaia complex. It was emplaced into the Precambrian metamorphic com- plexes of Juiz de Fora, Paraiba do Sul and the Aqungui Group [7,17]. The main lithological types are alkali plutonic rocks (nepheline syenites) with minor phonolitic dykes.
